title: Hecke L-functions
summary: $L$-functions of Hecke characters (Größencharaktere) on ideals of a number field. Hecke (1918) proved their analytic continuation and functional equation. Over $\mathbb Q$ they are Dirichlet $L$-functions.
why: The 2026 manuscript proves its zero-free half-plane for finite-order Hecke L-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and transfers it to Dirichlet L-functions.

prerequisites.title: Dirichlet L-functions and primes in progressions

timeline.title: Hecke L-functions
timeline.text: Defined $L$-functions of Größencharaktere and proved their functional equations.

timeline.title: Quasi-RH manuscript (7/8)
timeline.text: Claims every Dirichlet $L$-function is zero-free in $\operatorname{Re}s > \tfrac78$, using Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$, cubic theta sums and a Mellin continuation. Reported as Lean-verified.

title: Elliptic curves
summary: Curves $y^2 = x^3 + ax + b$ with a group law on their points. Hasse (1933) proved $|\#E(\mathbb F_p) - (p+1)| \le 2\sqrt p$. Wiles's 1995 proof of Fermat's Last Theorem went through elliptic curves.
why: The birth of modern arithmetic geometry; the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture is about them.
references: Silverman & Tate, Rational Points on Elliptic Curves

timeline.title: Fermat's Last Theorem
timeline.text: Proved via modularity of semistable elliptic curves.

title: Combinatorial number theory
summary: Questions about sets of integers where the argument is a counting or extremal one: pigeonhole on residues or exponent vectors, double counting, and constructions.
why: This is the native language of Erdős, and most of his problems below are stated in it.
references: Erdős & Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory
Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory

prerequisites.title: Primes and the fundamental theorem of arithmetic

title: Sumsets and additive combinatorics
summary: The study of $A+B = \{a+b\}$ for finite sets. Small doubling $|A+A| \le K|A|$ forces structure (Freiman), and Fourier analysis on $\mathbb Z/N$ measures how random a set is.
key_statements: |A+A| \le K|A| \Rightarrow A \subset \text{a generalised progression of size } O_K(|A|)
why: It connected number theory to ergodic theory and theoretical computer science, and produced the Green–Tao theorem.

timeline.title: Roth's theorem on 3-term progressions
timeline.text: Dense sets contain $3$-term progressions, by Fourier analysis on $\mathbb Z/N$.

timeline.title: 23 Erdős problems in the OpenAI release
timeline.text: Bloom listed the release's claims touching Erdős problems, including #3 via a 198-page quasipolynomial bound for Szemerédi's theorem whose Lean file proves only a weaker statement. He called it a summary of claims, not an endorsement.

title: Arithmetic Ramsey theory
summary: Colour the integers with finitely many colours; some colour class contains a given structure. Schur: a monochromatic $x+y=z$. Van der Waerden: arbitrarily long monochromatic progressions. Rado: exactly which linear systems are partition regular.
key_statements: \forall\, r\ \exists\, N:\ [1,N] = C_1\cup\cdots\cup C_r \Rightarrow \exists i,\ x,y,z\in C_i,\ x+y=z
why: Colouring statements are the qualitative form of density statements, and the gap between the two is where most of the difficulty lies.

timeline.title: Schur's theorem
timeline.text: Every finite colouring of $\mathbb N$ has a monochromatic solution of $x+y=z$, found while studying Fermat's equation modulo $p$.

timeline.title: Van der Waerden's theorem
timeline.text: Every finite colouring of $\mathbb N$ contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions.

title: Arithmetic progressions in dense sets
summary: Szemerédi (1975): a set of positive upper density contains arbitrarily long progressions. Quantitative bounds for $r_k(N)$, the largest progression-free subset of $[1,N]$, are the active question; Green and Tao found long progressions in the primes.
key_statements: \sum_{n\in A} \tfrac1n = \infty \overset{?}{\Rightarrow} A \text{ has arbitrarily long APs}
why: The Erdős–Turán problem (Erdős #3, a 5000-dollar prize) is the headline; an October 2026 AI-produced manuscript claims a bound strong enough to settle it.

timeline.title: Van der Waerden's theorem
timeline.text: Every finite colouring of $\mathbb N$ contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions.

timeline.title: Erdős and Turán on progressions
timeline.text: Conjectured that dense sets contain long progressions, the problem Szemerédi solved and whose reciprocal-sum form is Erdős #3.

timeline.title: Roth's theorem on 3-term progressions
timeline.text: Dense sets contain $3$-term progressions, by Fourier analysis on $\mathbb Z/N$.

timeline.title: Szemerédi's theorem
timeline.text: Every set of positive density contains arbitrarily long progressions.

timeline.title: The primes contain arbitrarily long progressions
timeline.text: A relative Szemerédi theorem applied to a pseudorandom majorant of the primes.

timeline.title: Strong bounds for 3-progressions
timeline.text: $r_3(N) \le N\exp(-c(\log N)^{1/12})$, close to Behrend's construction.

title: Sidon sets
summary: A set where all pairwise sums $a+b$ ($a\le b$) are distinct. In $[1,N]$ the maximum size is $\sqrt N + O(N^{1/4})$; whether the error is $O_\varepsilon(N^\varepsilon)$ is Erdős problem #30, with a 1000-dollar prize.
why: Sidon sets are the simplest structure whose extremal size is still not known to the right order of error.
references: Erdős & Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory

timeline.title: Sidon's question
timeline.text: Asked Erdős how dense a set with distinct pairwise sums can be, in work on Fourier series.
